newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling seen stable in jittery market.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling seen stable in jittery market.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was holding stable against the dollar on Wednesday in a generally jittery market, foreign exchange dealers said on Wednesday.

They said there had been swings in the shilling/dollar exchange, with the shilling weakening to as low as 55.50/70 against the dollar early on Wednesday before reversing the trend in the afternoon and closing at a stronger 54.70/55.10.

Traders said anxiety among oil companies had forced the shilling lower at close on Tuesday and opening on Wednesday but that was no longer the case and foreign inflows on Wednesday lifted the shilling back up.

"Since Monday, we have seen demand from importers and limited demand from foreign investors. On Tuesday, the market expected traditional inflows from exporters that did not materialise, so some people got into the market to cover their positions," said a dealer from a leading commercial bank.

"Basically there was heavy importer demand amid less supply from traditional exporters who supply most of forex inflows. That has been compensated for by continued inflows most of the day and the market is very calm," the dealer told Reuters.

One commercial bank put its shilling/dollar closing rate at 54.85/55.25 and said the market was calm on "healthy inflows". Another leading forex trade bank put its closing rates at a flat 55, firmer compared to 55.40/35 earlier on Wednesday.
"The trend is downwards for the dollar. The dollar should weaken further as foreign investor money comes in for Treasury bills," one chief dealer at a commercial bank told Reuters.

One commercial bank treasury told Reuters that there was anxiety in the market and as soon as a noticeable rush in buying was seen, especially from foreign investors, it caused a fast depreciation of the shilling. He cited Tuesday and Wednesday.
Many times that situation was not sustained, he said.
"The shilling is not moving fast and in spite of the anxiety, we have not seen any pullout of foreign investors. Instead, we are seeing some inflows of funds into the system, he added.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 55.05 versus the dollar compared to 54.27 on Tuesday.
Against the pound, the shilling was posted at a mean rate of 90.38 from 88.83. The dollar is the major trade currency on the Kenyan foreign exchange market.
Meanwhile the money market tightened marginally. Overnight rates were quoted at 10 percent from Tuesday's eight percent.

Many traders have linked market movement with jitters ahead of Kenya's parliamentary and presidential elections later in the year. A senior dealer said whereas there were some anxiety about the polls in the market, they were not sufficient tension yet to force any major movements either side.
